accuracy.reason: Correct reverse-proxy scope, connection/request distinction, sampled health and fail-open caveat, state versus affinity, drain deadline and durable idempotency boundaries.

evidence.quote: Health-based routing reduces exposure to failure; it cannot guarantee every request succeeds.

mechanisms.reason: Traces requests, snapshots of health, memory-only session failure, accepted-work drain and lost-response retry with atomic deduplication; diagrams explicitly avoid migrating unfinished work.

evidence.quote: Remove new assignments, handle existing connections and requests, then stop. Draining cannot promise zero interrupted work.

coherence.reason: Eight objectives connect routing unit to policies, readiness, state, removal/retry and whole-path availability; prerequisite transaction and connection concepts support transfer.

evidence.quote: Choose balancing for distribution or redundant serving; verify both entry-path availability and surviving capacity.

decisions.reason: Conditional balancing policies, shared state costs, bounded drain/retry, spare capacity and alternate entry requirements make deployment decisions concrete.

evidence.quote: Count requests or connections to select traffic, then measure the work those counts hide.

clarity.reason: Plain examples explain otherwise subtle L4 reuse, health sampling and response uncertainty without unneeded product configuration.

evidence.quote: Choose the routing unit and required HTTP visibility before choosing a balancing policy.

outcomes.reason: Traces both proxy directions, chooses L7 with readable/decrypted paths and separate backend TLS, explains connection-pinned L4 requests and when a single server suffices.

Explains turns/counts/weights and each limitation, conditionally favors connection-sensitive or weighted policy with measurement, rejects backend scaling past DB saturation and requires alternate reachable entry plus survivor headroom.

Distinguishes health response from useful DB-backed readiness, delayed/partial sampling, removal from new selection and inability to complete/undo/replay in-flight requests; notes all-unhealthy behavior.
Correct A-memory loss and B absence; affinity skews placement without copying or surviving state, shared store permits either backend but adds access/dependency costs.
Stops new assignments then waits boundedly for accepted work, manages existing connection/request acceptance, and admits deadline interruption without migration to B.

Explains unknown committed outcome, stable cross-backend durable key/result, unique reservation and effect/result in one transaction, duplicate recorded response, insufficiency of fresh keys/local memory and bounded delayed retry.

sourceChecks.claim: AWS ELB overview confirms distribution across targets and operation behind an entry; reverse-proxy return path is explicitly scoped rather than generalized to every balancer.

Azure overview distinguishes L7 path/SSL offload from L4 TCP/UDP. Network-load-balancer connection documentation confirms continued traffic on established connections, supporting request-versus-connection distinction.
NGINX documents round robin, least active connections and weighted shares, including uniform-work assumptions; those counts and configured shares do not measure arbitrary request cost.

AWS target-health documentation confirms periodic probes, thresholds and explicit all-unhealthy fail-open behavior; passing one sampled endpoint cannot prove unrelated DB capability or rescue accepted requests.
ASP.NET web-farm docs require sharing cross-node state, discuss same-node routing and distributed cache/database choices; session availability depends on those resources, not affinity alone.

ALB attributes documents draining and bounded deregistration delay. Official NLB attributes followup explicitly preserves existing non-idle connections and describes connection termination, validating the L4 drain caveat.

AWS idempotency article live-inspected earlier requires stable request identifiers and atomic durable token plus mutations, with equivalent returned result; retry delay/load limits also match Azure retry primary documentation.

Google SRE overload chapter explains finite backend capacity, unreliable request-count proxies and rejection/degradation under resource limits; Azure overview warns single regional routing resource is a failure point. Headroom and reachable alternate entry follow these path dependencies.
